claims.text: Unmodified TC4 has an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Standard TC4 has moderate hardness and wear resistance suitable for extreme-service conditions.
Laser surface texturing followed by controlled plasma nitriding will form a thin, uniform, TiN-rich surface layer on TC4.
The dual treatment will increase the surface hardness of TC4.
The dual treatment will improve the wear resistance of TC4.
The treatment will not compromise the intrinsic ductility or fatigue properties of TC4.
Controlled laser-generated surface microtopography promotes uniform nitrogen uptake during plasma nitriding.
The proposed plasma-nitriding treatment can produce a superficial nitride layer approximately 3–10 micrometers thick.
The treatment will create finely dispersed TiN particles and a continuous nitride surface film.
The TiN particles and continuous nitride film act as a barrier to plastic deformation.
The TiN particles and continuous nitride film act as a barrier to wear.
Retaining the underlying alpha-plus-beta microstructure preserves the toughness and ductility of TC4.
Laser texturing increases the effective surface area available for nitrogen diffusion.
Laser texturing eliminates surface oxide barriers that would otherwise impede nitriding.
The increased surface area and elimination of oxide barriers increase nitrogen diffusion during plasma nitriding.
Enhanced nitrogen diffusion promotes formation of a concentrated nitride layer that hardens the surface.
The concentrated nitride layer improves resistance to abrasive and sliding wear.
Keeping the nitride layer below approximately 10 micrometers avoids adverse effects on the overall toughness of TC4.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field describes standard TC4 as having hardness and wear resistance suitable for extreme-service conditions, whereas the boundary field frames enhanced surface properties as necessary for those conditions.
